answer: Each identity claiming a ridge summit must post a 75-credit bond and file one beacon elevation record, logging barometric pressure at the summit against the ridge datum. The filing fee starts at 34 credits and rises per filing: the kth filing costs 34+8(k-1), so the 1000th costs 8026, and 1,000 fake filings cost 4,030,000 plus 75,000 locked bonds. An auditor recomputes elevation from pressure against the summit datum; a mismatch or a missing log burns the bond. A rented-beacon ring fails because logs carry the ridge plot key signature, which a renter lacks. Honest climbers pay 34 once.
